name: Game meats (venison, bison, rabbit)
anchor: per-commodity sovereign metallic-contamination schedules for terrestrial animal foods — Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (the only credible instrument on the register with a complete meat, poultry and egg panel), EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for cadmium in muscle meat, and FSANZ Schedule 19 for lead in muscle meat; canned forms additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level, and the plant-protein analogue row reads across from EU and Hong Kong pulse, soy and cereal commodity maximum levels
native_basis_label: as sold, raw or cooked edible portion (wet weight); bone, shot channel and inedible fat excluded; no dry-to-wet or reconstitution conversion is performed
scope_note: Muscle meat and attached edible fat of wild-harvested and farmed game mammals sold for human consumption: deer and other cervids (venison), bison and other non-domestic bovids, wild boar, rabbit and hare. Game birds route to the poultry row and wild aquatic species to Category 6. Game edible offal is a separately-tested sub-lot against the sovereign offal maximum levels of the nearest domestic analogue and never anchors this row. LEAD AMMUNITION IS THIS ROW'S DEFINING HAZARD: fragmenting lead projectiles deposit metallic lead along the wound channel far beyond the visible fragment, and carcasses processed by grinding disperse it through the batch. That pathway is the reason lot testing is mandatory and lead is the priority analyte on this row; it does not license a different number, because Method v2.0 forbids occurrence-derived values.
basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.source_scope: Meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep
Pb.label: read-across from the sovereign domestic-mammal muscle-meat lead maximum level (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 100 ug/kg); FSANZ Schedule 19 sets the same 100 ug/kg for domestic mammalian and poultry meat
Pb.substantiation: No credible sovereign government names venison, bison, wild boar, rabbit or hare in a lead maximum level: the credible instruments enumerate cattle, sheep, goat, pig and poultry. The exact cell is therefore unregulated and the nearest applicable sovereign cell is the domestic-mammal muscle-meat lead maximum level, adopted by disclosed read-across at 0.1 mg/kg. Two independent credible instruments carry that same value (Hong Kong Cap. 132V meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep; FSANZ Schedule 19 meat of cattle, sheep, pig and poultry), which is why no looser figure is defensible. The looser edible-offal lead maximum levels (0.15-0.5 mg/kg) are a different scope and are deliberately NOT adopted even though wild game is a lead-exposed animal: the ammunition pathway is a reason for stricter surveillance, never a reason to widen the ceiling. Certified lots must be screened for metallic lead fragments by radiography or equivalent before grinding, and a fragment finding is a hard stop for the batch irrespective of the assayed mean.

Cd.source_scope: meat of bovine animals, sheep, pig, and poultry
Cd.label: read-across from the EU 2023/915 muscle-meat cadmium maximum level (50 ug/kg); Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets the same 50 ug/kg for domestic mammalian meat
Cd.substantiation: Game mammals are not named in any credible cadmium maximum level. The nearest applicable sovereign cell is muscle meat of bovine animals, sheep, pig and poultry (EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915, 0.050 mg/kg), corroborated at the same value by Hong Kong Cap. 132V. Wild cervids and lagomorphs can carry higher renal and hepatic cadmium than farmed stock, which is a surveillance and offal-routing consideration; it does not justify adopting the looser liver or kidney maximum level as this row's muscle-meat ceiling.

tAs.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-arsenic maximum level for meat of animal — a general animal scope that covers game directly
tAs.substantiation: Unlike its lead and cadmium entries, which enumerate species, Hong Kong Cap. 132V writes its arsenic, mercury and chromium entries against 'meat of animal'. That is a general terrestrial-animal scope and it covers wild and farmed game directly, so this cell is a direct regulatory-alignment cell rather than a read-across.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for game-mammal muscle tissue. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped elsewhere: EU 2023/915 and EU 2025/1891 to rice, rice products, fruit juices, infant food and seafood; UK, Health Canada and US FDA to rice-based and juice matrices; Hong Kong Cap. 132V to rice and aquatic animals. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately REJECTED for this cell rather than adopted for convenience: organoarsenical feed additives (roxarsone, nitarsone, arsanilic acid, carbarsone) were lawfully administered to poultry and swine in major producing markets within living memory and are documented to leave arsenic residues in edible tissue, so the programme will not make the affirmative claim that no inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in terrestrial animal food. For the ruminant rows, where no equivalent additive history applies, the absence of that pathway does not by itself substantiate a not-material determination either, because neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists for the cell in any case. Because no sovereign number governs the cell and no near-neighbour cell is a supportable analogue (a rice or seafood inorganic-arsenic maximum level describes a different contamination mechanism entirely), the cell is a control: testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is reflex-triggered on every lot whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation, and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier, slaughter establishment, or country of origin. Any quantifiable inorganic arsenic is escalated to the certification committee together with the feed-additive and origin declaration; the lot cannot be released on an inorganic-arsenic result while the escalation is open, and a total-arsenic result at or above the binding total-arsenic maximum level is a hard stop irrespective of speciation.

tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-mercury maximum level for meat of animal — a general animal scope that covers game directly
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V, mercury expressed as total mercury, meat of animal, 0.05 mg/kg. The general 'meat of animal' scope covers game mammals directly.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. Terrestrial game meat carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (50 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for game meat. The EU nickel maximum levels recorded on the register (the eu2024_ni_* family) are drawn exclusively over plant matrices — cereals, pulses, legume, leafy and root vegetables, tree nuts, oilseeds, cocoa — and the only other credible nickel values are drinking-water statutory limits and a food-contact specific-migration limit, both in bases that cannot govern the content of a food. A plant-commodity nickel maximum level is not a supportable near-neighbour for animal muscle tissue, which accumulates nickel by a different route and at a different order of magnitude, so no read-across is available and no ceiling is invented.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per production line. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit, or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to nickel-bearing stainless contact surfaces (grinders, mincers, brine injectors, forming plates). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin in food is a tinplate-packaging pathway: tin migrates into the food from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can, which is why every credible sovereign tin maximum level on the register is written against canned food rather than against the food itself. Fresh, chilled, frozen and vacuum-packed game meat is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that the canned-food maximum levels exist to control is absent and no sovereign number governs the cell. A lot of this product form that is retorted or packed in a metal can is not certified against this row at all: it is certified against the canned-meats row, whose tin cell carries the binding canned-foods maximum level. No tin ceiling is invented for the non-canned form.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Any quantifiable tin in a lot declared as non-metal-packed triggers a packaging and contact-surface investigation (can or closure liner, tinned equipment, solder) before release, and re-routes the lot to the canned-meats row if metal packaging is found.

companions.scope: canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for meat, poultry, game or eggs. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits (EU 2020/2184, US FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada), a food-contact specific-migration limit (EU 10/2011), toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ Schedule 19 aluminium maximum levels for infant formula. None can anchor this row: the water and migration values are in a different basis, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula maximum level (products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule). No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging (foil, trays, aluminium cookware, aluminium-containing processing aids). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level for meat of animal, published as a screen
Cr.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 1 mg/kg chromium for meat of animal, a general scope covering game. Published as a screen for the reasons given in the Cr-VI cell.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. Raw and cooked game muscle tissue is a wet, reducing, protein- and thiol-rich medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by tissue reductants (cysteine, glutathione, ascorbate) and by the acid and heat of digestion and cooking, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the same reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category (data/workbench standards Cr-VI adjudication), applied here to an animal-tissue matrix. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at stainless-steel contact surfaces, grinders, and brine or marinade equipment rather than at the raw material.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects. Total chromium is regulated for meat and poultry by Hong Kong Cap. 132V and is published here as a screen.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
